([[Fort Erie, Ontario]]) | team1 = [[NBA G League Ignite]] | years1 = [[2022-23 NBA G League season|2022]]–present | highlights = * [[NBA G League]] Next Up Game ([[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{CAN}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship|2019 Brazil]]|[[Canada men's national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Leonard Miller''' (born November 26, 2003) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]]. ==Early life and high school career== Miller was born in [[Scarborough, Toronto|Scarborough]], [[Ontario]] and played basketball, [[volleyball]] and [[golf]] during his childhood.{{cite web |title=Leonard Miller |url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/leonard-miller |publisher=Pro Insight |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=November 23, 2021}} He played basketball for [[Thornlea Secondary School]] in [[Thornhill, Ontario]], helping the team win the National Junior Circuit title in March 2019.{{cite web |last1=Mikre |first1=Mickias |title=National Jr. Circuit Championships Recap – Thornlea crowned as 2019 Champions |url=https://northpolehoops.com/2019/03/06/national-jr-circuit-championships-recap-thornlea-crowned-as-2019-champions/ |publisher=North Pole Hoops |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=March 6, 2019}} Miller transferred to [[Wasatch Academy]] in [[Mount Pleasant, Utah]] to face stronger competition but received limiting playing time. He transferred to Victory Rock Prep in [[Bradenton, Florida]] before missing several months with a broken right wrist in November 2020 that required surgery.{{cite web |last1=Osman |first1=Libaan |title=How Scarborough’s Leonard Miller became this year’s most intriguing NBA draft prospect |url=https://www.thestar.com/news/gta/2022/05/27/how-scarboroughs-leonard-miller-became-this-years-most-intriguing-nba-draft-prospect.html?rf |website=[[Toronto Star]] |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=May 27, 2022}} Miller opted to play a [[postgraduate year|postgraduate]] season at Fort Erie International Academy in [[Fort Erie, Ontario]] and had no college offers at the time he made the decision.{{cite web |last1=Kalbrosky |first1=Bryan |title=Leonard Miller is suddenly the most intriguing NBA draft prospect, but it's what he does next that matters most |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2022/05/nba-draft-leonard-miller-kentucky-arizona-g-league-ignite-overtime-elite |publisher=For The Win |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=May 6, 2022}} He became the team's star player and received over 25 offers from college programs. Miller led Fort Erie to an Ontario Scholastic Basketball Association title and was named league [[most valuable player]]. He was selected to play for the World Team in the [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last1=Pilgrim |first1=Jack |title=Leonard Miller among top participants at Nike Hoop Summit |url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/leonard-miller-among-top-participants-at-nike-hoop-summit/ |publisher=On3 |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=April 6, 2022}} On April 23, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Backus |first1=Will |title=Leonard Miller, uncommitted prospect in 2022 class, declares for NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Leonard-Miller-uncommitted-prospect-in-2022-class-declares-for-NBA-Draft-186654105/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=April 23, 2022}} ===Recruiting=== Miller was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and a four-star recruit by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]]. On May 31, 2022, he announced that he would pursue professional options instead of playing [[college basketball]].{{cite web |last1=Siegel |first1=Brett |title=Potential First-Round Pick Leonard Miller To Skip College, Play Professionally |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/draft/potential-2022-nba-draft-pick-leonard-miller-to-skip-college-and-play-professionally |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=June 11, 2022 |date=May 31, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===NBA G League Ignite (2022–present)=== On September 7, 2022, Miller signed a contract with the [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite web|url= https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/09/07/nba-g-league-ignite-mojave-king-leonard-miller-contracts/|title=Mojave King, Leonard Miller officially signs contracts with G League Ignite|date=September 7, 2022|access-date=September 7, 2022 }} He was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.{{Cite web |title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game |access-date=March 8, 2023 |website=NBA G League}} ==National team career== Miller won a silver medal with Canada at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil, averaging 4.2 points per game.{{cite web |title=Leonard Miller (CAN)'s profile – FIBA U16 Americas Championship 2019 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/u16americas/2019/player/Leonard-Miller |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=June 11, 2022}} ==Personal life== Miller's older brother, [[Emanuel Miller (basketball)|Emanuel]], played college basketball for [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] before transferring to [[TCU Horned
